**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject QMUL kernels with non-dense SSBO offsets**

This QMUL replay receives only the three bindings and then treats both inputs and the output as dense texel arrays starting at the descriptor offsets, so texel `gid` always represents `load_ssbo(..., gid * sizeof(vec4))`. I checked `r300_nir_detect_qmul_pattern`: it records only bindings and does not validate the `load_ssbo`/`store_ssbo` byte-offset expressions, so a canonical Hamilton kernel such as `out[gid] = q1[gid + 1] * q2[gid]` is still marked `pl->qmul.is_qmul` and reaches this path, but replay computes `q1[gid] * q2[gid]` and silently writes wrong results. Please validate the offset/index shape before using this replay or leave these kernels unsupported.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid half-quantizing unrestricted FP32 QMUL results**

For every accepted QMUL kernel this path renders the product to `PIPE_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` and then unpacks it into the shader's `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` storage buffer. Because the detector admits the canonical four-`fdot4` shape without any operand/result range or relaxed-precision check, values that the original FP32 storage-buffer store could carry but FP16 cannot represent (for example a component above 65504, or any value needing more than FP16 precision) are rounded or become infinity before being written back. That makes valid-looking detected shaders produce numerically different SSBO contents; either constrain the admitted domain to FP16-safe results or avoid routing general FP32 QMUL stores through an FP16 render target.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Map only the actual QMUL output byte count**

When a QMUL dispatch has more than one raster row and the invocation count is not a multiple of 2048, `derive_raster_extent()` pads the last row, but this map request still covers `width * height * buf_bs` bytes from the output SSBO. The new unpack loop correctly stops at `total_invocations`, yet an exactly-sized output buffer (for example 2049 `vec4`s) is mapped as 4096 `vec4`s before that clamp can help, so replay can fail or touch a range past the descriptor/resource. Use `total_invocations * buf_bs` for the output buffer range while still reading the padded RT rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Populate timeline semaphore properties before advertising**

When `VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore` is exposed here, `VkPhysicalDeviceTimelineSemaphoreProperties::maxTimelineSemaphoreValueDifference` remains zero because `r300vk_physical_device_init_properties()` starts from `memset(props, 0, ...)` and this patch adds no assignment for that property (repo-wide `rg maxTimelineSemaphoreValueDifference` finds no r300vk setter). Apps that query the required timeline property can treat every signal/wait that advances from 0 to 1 as outside the advertised limit, so the extension is not self-consistent until this is set to the supported range.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Set robustness2 alignment properties for the extension**

Advertising `VK_EXT_robustness2` makes `VkPhysicalDeviceRobustness2PropertiesEXT` queryable, but both `robustStorageBufferAccessSizeAlignment` and `robustUniformBufferAccessSizeAlignment` still come back as zero because properties are zero-initialized and r300vk never assigns them (checked with `rg robustStorageBufferAccessSizeAlignment src/amd/r300/vulkan/r300vk`). These fields are required power-of-two limits for the extension, so clients/tests that query the extension properties will see invalid limits even though the extension is reported.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not advertise nullDescriptor until UBO slots are cleared**

With `nullDescriptor` enabled, a pipeline that reads a null uniform-buffer descriptor after a previous draw bound a real UBO can read the previous buffer instead of zero: `r300vk_bind_one_stage_ubo()` only `return`s when `desc->buf.buffer` is NULL and never clears the Gallium constant buffer slot (see `r300vk_queue.c:589-591`). This violates the advertised null-descriptor behavior for uniform buffers and can leak stale descriptor data into zink/unbound-buffer draws.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a point sync type accepted by vk_sync_timeline**

This wraps `r300vk_cpu_sync_type` in `vk_sync_timeline_get_type()`, but the timeline helper validates that the point type has `VK_SYNC_FEATURE_GPU_MULTI_WAIT` in addition to binary/GPU/CPU wait/reset support (`vk_sync_timeline.c:53-60`), and `r300vk_cpu_sync_type` does not advertise that feature (`r300vk_cpu_sync.c:128-134`). In debug builds, creating a timeline semaphore through the newly advertised extension will hit that assertion, so the advertised timeline path is unusable until the point sync type satisfies the helper's required feature set or a different point type is used.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the new extensions behind Vulkan 1.1 support**

Both extensions added here are registered with a `VK_VERSION_1_1` dependency in `src/vulkan/registry/vk.xml`, but r300vk still reports `R300VK_API_VERSION` as Vulkan 1.0 and `vk_physical_device_init()` copies this table verbatim without enforcing version dependencies. On this 1.0 device, apps or validation that honor extension dependencies can reject the exposed `VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore`/`VK_EXT_robustness2` set even before reaching the feature checks, so these should be withheld until the driver can advertise the required API level or a conformant dependency path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pack the rotated vec3 back into RGB lanes**

When this QROTATE FS is used with the existing two-in/one-out replay path, the copy-back preserves RGBA order (`util_format_unpack_rgba` in `r300vk_two_in_one_out_dispatch_replay`), but `rotated` is still a quaternion in `(w,x,y,z)` layout. For an identity quaternion and input vector `(1,2,3)`, this stores `(0,1,2,3)` into the output buffer, shifting the rotated vector out of RGB instead of returning `(1,2,3,...)`. Store channels 1..3 (and an explicit alpha/scalar value) rather than the whole quaternion result.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't advertise packed ZS attachments before binding them**

When `VK_FORMAT_D24_UNORM_S8_UINT` is mapped to an r300 ZS format here, `r300vk_get_format_properties()` now advertises `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_2_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_BIT` and `vkCreateImage` accepts `DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT` usage for it, but the render-pass path still records only the first color attachment and `r300vk_replay_begin_render_pass()` never sets `fb.zsbuf` or any depth/stencil state (the command-buffer header also says depth/stencil aspects are intentionally ignored). Any app that actually uses the newly advertised D24/S8 attachment will render with depth/stencil silently disabled, so this format should stay unadvertised as a DS attachment until the ZS framebuffer path exists.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate D24 transfer reads until the aspect is repacked**

The new mapping makes these packed depth formats pass the existing format-property and image-usage gates for `TRANSFER_SRC`, but `r300vk_copy_image_region_to_buffer()` only does a raw row `memcpy` from the Gallium resource. For a depth-aspect copy of `VK_FORMAT_D24_UNORM_S8_UINT`, this returns the `S8_UINT_Z24_UNORM` storage order (stencil in the low byte, depth in bits 8..31) even though the Vulkan buffer layout requires D24 in the low 24 bits, as the added TODO notes. Please either withhold `TRANSFER_SRC` for the remapped D24 formats or implement the repack before advertising them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind sampled views using the selected aspect format**

For depth/stencil image views, `vk_image_view_init()` keeps `iv->vk.format` as the full image format and puts the aspect-specific format in `iv->vk.view_format` (for example a stencil-only view of D24/S8 becomes S8). Now that D24/S8 is advertised as sampled and reaches this path, binding a stencil-aspect view still creates a sampler view as `PIPE_FORMAT_S8_UINT_Z24_UNORM`, so the shader's R component reads the depth channel instead of the selected stencil aspect. Use the view format, or reject stencil-aspect sampled views, before exposing sampled D24/S8.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject shifted unary SSBO accesses**

For QCONJ/QNORM kernels whose arithmetic matches but whose SSBO offsets are not the implicit per-texel `gid` mapping (for example `out[gid] = conj(in[gid + 1])` or a shifted/scattered store), this gate still admits the pattern because it only checks the number of loads/stores and never validates `load->src[1]` or `store->src[2]`. The replay path samples and writes the current raster texel, so these kernels are silently executed as if the load and store offsets were the unshifted identity mapping.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate QCONJ replay on f32x4 elements**

When the matched QCONJ kernel operates on `f16vec4` SSBO elements, the classifier still admits it and the detector can match the same sign-flip arithmetic, but this replay path always treats the buffer as `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT`. In that case each shader element is 8 bytes while the replay reads and writes 16 bytes per invocation, so dispatches can consume adjacent elements and overwrite twice the intended output range instead of falling back.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid FP16 round-trip for QCONJ f32 results**

For matched `f32vec4` QCONJ kernels with components that are not exactly representable as binary16 (for example `1.0001f`, small subnormals, or values above 65504), this path renders through `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` and only then unpacks back to the kernel's FP32 output buffer. A conjugate is just an FP32 sign flip and should preserve the input magnitude, so this silently rounds or clamps otherwise valid f32 outputs instead of rejecting the pattern or using an exact carrier.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit OMUL copies to logical invocation count**

For OMUL dispatches whose invocation count is not a multiple of 2048, `derive_raster_extent` pads the raster grid (for example 2049 invocations becomes 2048x2), but this call asks `r300vk_identity_map_wrap_input_as_sampler_view` to copy `width * height` RGBA32 elements from each input buffer. A correctly sized SSBO only contains `total` elements, so the new OMUL path can fail the buffer map or read past the descriptor for valid dispatch sizes above one row; the copy-back in `omul_run_pass` uses the same padded width for the mapped output range.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve lower OMUL half when outputs alias**

When the two output descriptors are different bindings into the same `VkBuffer` (for example a contiguous octonion result with separate lower/upper offsets), the second `omul_run_pass` maps the same pipe resource with `PIPE_MAP_DISCARD_WHOLE_RESOURCE`, which may orphan or invalidate the lower-half data written by the first pass. Vulkan storage-buffer descriptors can alias the same buffer, so this two-pass path should avoid whole-resource discard when writing one half after the other.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject OMUL kernels with one output binding**

When both OMUL stores target the same storage-buffer binding (for example one octonion output buffer with lower/upper halves at different offsets), the detector still marks the shader as `is_omul`. The replay path ignores the stores' NIR offsets and assumes two output descriptors, so captured same-binding metadata makes the upper pass overwrite the lower at the same descriptor offset, while opaque metadata can write the upper half to an unrelated sixth storage buffer instead of rejecting the unsupported shape.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate submit-boundary sync failures**

When a mapped owns_buffer needs submit-boundary coherence, `r300vk_sync_owns_buffer` can return `VK_ERROR_MEMORY_MAP_FAILED` or an allocation-bound error, but this new list walker drops the result and `r300vk_queue_driver_submit` can continue and signal success with a stale bound resource. This affects low-memory/map-failure paths and malformed/oversized bindings; the submit path should return the first sync error just like Flush/Invalidate already do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track the mapped subrange before syncing it at submit**

For coherent memory mapped with a non-zero `vkMapMemory` offset or a smaller-than-allocation size, this new submit sync still asks `r300vk_sync_owns_buffer` to copy the whole allocation while `mem->map_ptr` is only the pointer returned for that mapped box. In those cases it copies from/to the wrong allocation offsets and can read or write beyond the mapped range; the memory object needs to remember the current map offset/size and sync only that window.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync mapped linear images before GPU access**

When a linear image is bound to an already-mapped host-coherent allocation, `BindImageMemory2` records `bound_image_tile`, but this new submit-boundary sync only pulls that tile on submit exit and deliberately skips the submit-entry host→image direction. Apps that write a mapped linear image and then submit a copy or shader read without an explicit flush are valid for the advertised `HOST_COHERENT` type, but the GPU will still see the stale tile because those host writes are never uploaded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Layer the WSI physical-device entrypoints**

Initializing `wsi_device` here and advertising `VK_KHR_surface` is not enough because the physical-device dispatch table above is still built only from `r300vk_physical_device_entrypoints`; the common WSI surface-query functions live in `wsi_physical_device_entrypoints` (checked with `rg --fixed-strings wsi_physical_device_entrypoints src/`, and both lavapipe and Terakan layer it into their physical-device dispatch). In any X11 WSI path that calls `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR` or `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR` before creating the swapchain, the advertised extension still resolves to a missing/null physical-device entrypoint, so presentation setup fails before this new software swapchain path is reached.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Advertise the linear usages that CreateImage now accepts**

This now permits linear images with `COLOR_ATTACHMENT` and `SAMPLED` usage, but `r300vk_get_format_properties` still reports `linearTilingFeatures` as only transfer src/dst. For clients or WSI code paths that validate a linear swapchain image with `vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2` before creation, the query rejects the same usage that `CreateImage` accepts, so `wsi_device.wants_linear` can still make swapchain setup fail even though the create path was relaxed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep WSI out of the loader-only build**

In the loader-only configuration where `-Dr300vk-gallium-backend=false`, Meson still compiles `r300vk_instance.c` and `r300vk_physical_device.c` but only adds `idep_vulkan_wsi` inside the Gallium-backed block (checked `src/amd/r300/vulkan/r300vk/meson.build`: base files/deps at lines 19-30, WSI dep at lines 68-70). This new include and the new `wsi_*` symbol references therefore lack the WSI include path/link dependency in that supported configuration, breaking the build that the Meson comments say should continue to work.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard X11 surface extensions by platform support**

These XCB/XLIB extensions are advertised unconditionally, but Mesa only defines the corresponding common WSI entrypoints when the build enables the X11 platform (`VK_USE_PLATFORM_XCB_KHR` / `VK_USE_PLATFORM_XLIB_KHR`; checked `src/vulkan/meson.build`), and neighboring drivers such as Terakan guard these bits with the same platform macros. On a non-X11 Vulkan build, an app can now enable `VK_KHR_xcb_surface` or `VK_KHR_xlib_surface` and then resolve/call a surface-create entrypoint that was never compiled into the WSI table.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Filter unsupported swapchain image usages**

Enabling `VK_KHR_swapchain` through unmodified common WSI makes X11 surface caps report `wsi_caps_get_image_usage()`, which includes `STORAGE` and `INPUT_ATTACHMENT`, but r300vk's image create path still rejects those usage bits. In applications that request a swapchain image usage advertised by `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR`, `vkCreateSwapchainKHR` can therefore fail later with `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` even though the surface caps said the usage was supported; this needs a driver surface-capability override/filter like other limited WSI drivers use.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not present from an unsynced linear image map**

Setting `wants_linear` makes common X11 CPU WSI take the no-blit path: it maps the swapchain memory before `BindImageMemory` and `x11_present_to_x11_sw` later reads `image->base.cpu_map` directly. In r300vk that map-before-bind linear-image case keeps the host map on a separate lazy buffer while `BindImageMemory2` only records the image tile and relies on `InvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` to copy tile contents back, but WSI never invalidates before present, so rendered swapchain images are presented from stale or blank host memory.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use American English spelling**

`AGENTS.md` requires American English in new or modified source comments, but this added comment uses `colour-attachment`. Please spell this as `color-attachment` so the checked-in source comment conforms to the repository instructions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fall back when MRT shader compilation fails**

On r300, `create_fs_state` does not reliably return NULL for fragment compiler failures unless `report_compile_error` is set; `r300_create_fs_state` otherwise installs a dummy shader and returns a non-NULL CSO after recording `fs->shader->error`. For any screen that passes the RT/FP16 capability gate but cannot compile this larger two-output MRT program (instruction/temporary/output limits, or `RADEON_DEBUG=dummysh` behavior), `pl->fs_cso_mrt` becomes non-NULL and dispatch line 2081 will prefer route B, producing dummy output instead of using the working two-pass route A. Set `report_compile_error` for this optional shader or otherwise detect the dummy/error case before using the pointer as the route gate.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry the two-pass route when MRT allocation fails**

When route B is selected, `omul_run_mrt_pass` must allocate both FP16 render targets at once before drawing, whereas route A allocates and frees one target per half. On memory-constrained runs or large dispatches where the second target/map fails but a single target would still fit, this path returns failure immediately instead of falling back to the existing two-pass implementation, so a dispatch that previously could complete via route A now fails solely because the fast path was attempted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve aliased output halves in MRT copies**

When the two output descriptors refer to different ranges of the same VkBuffer, this passes the same `pipe_resource` twice to `omul_run_mrt_pass`. That helper copies each render target through `omul_copy_fp16_rt_to_buffer`, whose `buffer_map` uses `PIPE_MAP_DISCARD_WHOLE_RESOURCE`, so the second half copy can discard the bytes just written for the first half. This affects valid OADD/OSUB layouts that bind the low/high halves as separate storage-buffer descriptors into one buffer; the analogous OCONJ call has the same aliasing hazard.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject swizzled dot operands for ONORM**

For ONORM this only checks that both `fdot4` operands come from the same load SSA def, but it never verifies either dot source uses the identity swizzle. A shader such as `dot(a.xxxx, a.xxxx) + dot(b, b)` therefore matches the ONORM fast path, while the replay shader always computes `dot(a.xyzw, a.xyzw) + dot(b.xyzw, b.xyzw)`, producing different results for those inputs; the existing QNORM detector avoids this by checking each dot source swizzle.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject partially captured SSBO bindings**

When any one binding is nonzero this skips the positional fallback for the whole octonion kernel, so any binding source the detector could not constant-fold remains `0` and is resolved as descriptor binding 0. That misroutes kernels that mix constant SSBO bindings with a dynamic descriptor-array binding (for example one OADD operand indexed dynamically) instead of rejecting or resolving the dynamic slot, so replay can read or write the wrong buffer whenever that dynamic index is not binding 0.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject offset-shifted octonion operands**

This recognizes OADD/OSUB solely from the value SSA graph and never checks that the matched loads and stores use the same element offset. A kernel such as `o_lo[gid] = a[gid + 1] + c[gid]` still satisfies these operand checks, but the replay path samples every input at the same raster texel and writes the current output texel, so the fast path silently computes a different elementwise operation; the same missing offset gate exists in the new OCONJ/ONORM detectors.

For pipelines where `logicOpEnable` and the attachment's `blendEnable` are both true, this preserves `blend_enable` in the Gallium CSO even though Vulkan says logical operations make blending of all attachments behave as disabled. r300g consumes this CSO by programming blend when `rt[0].blend_enable` is set and separately programming the ROP when `logicop_enable` is set (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_state.c:517` and `:600`), so such valid pipelines can combine the blend equation with the logic op instead of applying only the logic op.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip logic ops for float and sRGB attachments**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate dynamic strides on pipeline state**

When a command buffer uses `vkCmdBindVertexBuffers2` with `pStrides` but the bound graphics pipeline did not declare `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VERTEX_INPUT_BINDING_STRIDE`, the vertex-input stride must remain the pipeline-static value. I checked `r300vk_capture_dynamic_state`, and it records other dynamic states but no vertex-stride bit, so this branch patches the vertex-element CSO solely from `vb_strides_mask`. That makes valid static-stride pipelines fetch and clamp vertices using bind-time strides, producing the wrong layout whenever an app passes different `pStrides` for another dynamic pipeline or just uses the 1.3 bind entry point. Track the pipeline's dynamic-stride declaration and only patch/use `vb_strides` for those pipelines.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce pSizes for indexed vertex fetches**

This records the `pSizes` range, but it is only consumed by `r300vk_robust_vertex_count` in the non-indexed draw branch; the indexed path only clamps the index-buffer range before calling Gallium. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't clamp vertex count from instance-rate ranges**

Passing the pSizes-shortened `vb_sizes` into `r300vk_robust_vertex_count` makes every binding cap `draw.count` as if it advances per vertex; that helper only sees `vertex_binding_mask` and never checks the binding input rate or `instance_divisor` stored in the vertex elements. When the new unary detector matches a 32-bit float scalar kernel such as `d[i] = d[i] * 2.0 + 1.0`, this delegation reuses `r300vk_identity_map_replay_format`, whose default carrier is `PIPE_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` unless the shape is vec4x32 with the explicit FP32x4 opt-in. Because a scalar float element is also 4 bytes, the existing block-size check does not reject it; the replay samples the float buffer bytes as RGBA8 normalized color and writes UNORM bytes back instead of a float result. The binary-map replay already has a `value_is_float && value_bit_size == 32` path (checked with `rg --fixed-strings value_is_float src/amd/r300/vulkan/r300vk/`); the unary path needs an equivalent format/conversion path or must reject these kernels rather than silently corrupting the compute output.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-uniform vector affine constants**

For vec2/vec3/vec4 unary maps with per-component constants, this helper only reads the first swizzled component and the synthesized FS later repeats that scalar as `{c0,c0,c0,c0}` / `{c1,c1,c1,c1}`. A shader like `out[i] = in[i] * vec4(1,2,3,4) + vec4(5,6,7,8)` therefore matches the unary pattern but computes every lane with the X constants. Please either verify all live lanes of the constant source are identical before accepting the pattern or carry per-lane constants into the generated fragment shader.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve same-buffer unary bindings**

For an in-place unary kernel with a single storage-buffer binding, such as the motivating `d[i] = d[i] * 2 + 1`, the post-explicit-IO detector leaves both captured bindings at the default `0`, and these assignments mirror that `0/0` pair into `identity_map`. The delegated identity replay interprets `0/0` as “unknown” and falls back to finding the first two storage-buffer bindings, so a one-binding descriptor set returns `layout-has-fewer-than-two-storage-buffers` and the dispatch still fails instead of updating the buffer in place. The unary path needs to distinguish a real same-buffer binding from missing metadata before delegating to the identity replay.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject swizzled unary inputs**

For vector unary maps, this helper treats any ALU source whose SSA def is the load as `load` without checking the source swizzle, but the synthesized fragment shader samples the input texture in natural XYZW order. A kernel like `out[i] = in[i].yxzw * 2.0 + 1.0` therefore matches the unary pattern and is replayed as if it were `in[i].xyzw`, producing lane-swapped results. Please require identity swizzles on the live lanes before admitting the pattern, or carry the swizzle into the generated FS.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require gid-based offsets before admitting CONSTFILL**

For kernels that store a compile-time constant to a fixed or otherwise non-elementwise offset, this still sets `is_const_fill` even though the shader only writes that address (for example the added test builder uses offset `0`). Since the detector never validates `store[0]->src[2]` against `gl_GlobalInvocationID`/the per-element offset before declaring a whole-buffer clear, a future CONSTFILL lowering would replace `out[0] = C` or a constant header write with an RB3D clear of every output element.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject vec4 fills until all components are represented**

When the stored value has four 32-bit components, this records only `lc->value[0]` in the four-byte clear color but still admits the store and reports `value_components == 4`. A shader like the new vec4 test (`0x01010101, 0x02020202, ...`) writes 16 bytes per element, while the CONSTFILL metadata can only drive a 4-byte RGBA8 clear from the first component, so any lowering using this detection would fill the output with repeated component 0 bytes instead of the requested vec4.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject sub-32-bit fills before using an RGBA8 clear**

For 8- or 16-bit SSBO stores, this still admits the kernel as CONSTFILL but expands the value into a four-channel RGBA8 clear with zeroed high bytes. Those shaders write one or two bytes per invocation, not a four-byte texel, so lowering this metadata through an RB3D clear/readback path would either overwrite adjacent packed elements or produce a buffer with the wrong per-element stride unless a separate narrow packing path is added.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**question (bug_risk):** The multitap gather walker silently fails when exceeding `R300_MULTITAP_MAX_TAPS`; consider making this limit more explicit.

In `multitap_add_tree_taps`, hitting `R300_MULTITAP_MAX_TAPS` causes an immediate `-1`:
```c
if (*tap_count >= R300_MULTITAP_MAX_TAPS)
   return -1;
```
so reductions with more than 8 taps are rejected outright, not just capped while still reporting the full tap count. Please clarify in the comment whether higher-tap kernels are intentionally unsupported and rejected at this threshold (and say so explicitly), or adjust the logic to track the true leaf count separately from the bounded `taps[]` array so `tap_total` can still reflect the real size for the `tap_total != 3` check.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the duplicate const-fill pattern type**

When `r300_compute_admission.h` is included, this new `struct r300_compute_const_fill_pattern` collides with the existing definition later in the same header (around line 715, with `const_value`/`output_ssbo_binding_valid` members). C does not permit redefining the same struct tag in one translation unit, so this breaks every r300/r300vk file that includes the admission header before the new replay path can build.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the duplicate const-fill detector**

This adds a second global definition of `r300_nir_detect_const_fill_pattern` in the same C file; the file already defines that function later (around line 3385). Any build of `r300_compute_admission.c` will fail with a redefinition error, so the CONSTFILL admission path cannot be compiled as submitted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the duplicate pipeline member**

This new `const_fill` member duplicates the existing `struct r300_compute_const_fill_pattern const_fill;` later in `struct r300vk_pipeline` (around line 173). C rejects duplicate member names within a struct, so including `r300vk_pipeline.h` now breaks the r300vk build even if the detector/header duplicates are fixed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the duplicate const-fill replay**

This introduces another global definition of `r300vk_const_fill_dispatch_replay`, but `r300vk_identity_map.c` already defines the same function later in the file (around line 4482). C rejects duplicate function definitions, so the r300vk translation unit will fail to compile independently of the admission/header duplicates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Map only the dispatched elements, not the padded raster**

For dispatch sizes that do not exactly fill the derived 2D extent (for example 2049 invocations becomes a 2048×2 RT), this maps `width * height * 4` bytes even though the shader only writes `total * 4` bytes. If the output SSBO allocation/range is sized for the actual dispatch, the padded map can run past the valid buffer range and turn an otherwise valid const-fill into a failed no-op; the later `copy_rows` call already clips to `total`, so the mapped buffer box should be sized the same way.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate CONSTFILL replay on coordinate-indexed stores**

When this branch makes CONSTFILL dispatches executable, any one-store/no-load shader with a constant value is bulk-filled as a contiguous `out[gid] = C` range, but the detector does not verify the store offset at all: `r300_nir_detect_const_fill_pattern` only checks that `store->src[0]` is constant/full-width and never examines `store->src[2]`, while the classifier admits all `store_ssbo` shapes. A valid constant-store kernel such as `out[gid * 2] = 0` will therefore be misdetected and this replay path will overwrite elements `0..N-1` contiguously instead of only the even indices, silently corrupting buffer contents rather than falling through to the unknown-shape no-op.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass the full Gallium clear signature**

This `pipe->clear` call is missing the `color_clear_mask` and `stencil_clear_mask` parameters; `struct pipe_context::clear` in this tree takes eight arguments (`pipe, buffers, color_clear_mask, stencil_clear_mask, scissor_state, color, depth, stencil`), as shown by the other r300vk callers. As written, this translation unit will fail to compile before the CONSTFILL replay path can be tested.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject vector constants until their lanes are packed**

The replay accepts any constant whose total element size is 4 bytes, but the later clear color is built only from `pl->const_fill.value[0]`. For a full-width `u8vec4` or `u16vec2` store, `element_bytes` is still 4, so the path runs and writes the first component's bytes plus zeros instead of the four stored bytes from all lanes; until the lanes are packed into RGBA, this should be limited to scalar 32-bit fills.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Discard only the mapped fill range**

For CONSTFILL dispatches that write a subrange of a larger/storage-offset buffer, mapping with `PIPE_MAP_DISCARD_WHOLE_RESOURCE` can invalidate bytes outside the shader's written range; Gallium documents this flag as discarding all backing memory for the resource. The old CPU const-fill path used `PIPE_MAP_DISCARD_RANGE`, and this replay should do the same so unrelated buffer contents survive when only `total` elements are filled.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track vector lanes separately in index walk**

For vectorized stored values such as `store_ssbo(vec2(gid, gid * 4))`, this visited check keys only on the `nir_def`, so the first path that reaches the `vecN` result wins and later index-derived lanes are skipped. When that vector def reaches `store_ssbo` as the value, the classifier records a single stride/offset even though another written lane may have a larger affine coefficient, so the intended FP24 dispatch guard can admit grids where one stored lane exceeds the exact-integer range. The walk needs to distinguish components or conservatively merge conflicting lane states instead of dropping revisits.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard non-finite float constants before casting**

When a shader stores an affine expression with a non-finite float constant, such as `float(gl_GlobalInvocationIndex) + NaN`, this check casts the constant to `uint64_t` before proving it is finite and in range. Floating-to-integer conversion of NaN/Inf or an out-of-range value is undefined in C during pipeline classification, so these operands should be rejected with `isfinite()`/range checks before any cast.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip raster exactness for CPU const-fill dispatches**

For `CONSTFILL` pipelines that do not consume the index, this new global gate rejects any dispatch above the 2048x2048 raster fold before reaching the `pl->const_fill.is_const_fill` branch. That replay path is a CPU buffer fill rather than a draw, so a large valid `out[gid] = C` dispatch now becomes a logged no-op and leaves the output buffer unchanged even though no FP24/raster index identity is involved.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require gid-addressed stores before accepting affine iota**

This detector only proves that the stored value is an affine function of the invocation index; it never verifies that the `store_ssbo` offset is `gid * 4`. A kernel such as `out[0] = gl_GlobalInvocationIndex` has one integer store, zero loads, and a VALUE_AFFINE stored value, so it is admitted as AFFINE_IOTA, but the replay writes `out[gid] = gid` across the whole buffer instead of only the single addressed element.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let atomic reductions pass the index gate**

For admitted blend-accumulation kernels such as `atomicAdd(out[gid & mask], in[gid])`, the index reaches an `ssbo_atomic` offset; `r300_nir_classify_index_consumption()` does not treat atomics as address-only consumers, so it reports VALUE_GENERAL and this new pre-dispatch gate returns success as a no-op before the `blend_acc_reduction` replay branch can run. Those histogram-style reductions therefore stop producing output despite having a dedicated replay path below.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict affine iota to the flat global index**

This accepts any VALUE_AFFINE index value from the generic classifier, including stores of `gl_GlobalInvocationID.x` or `gl_LocalInvocationIndex`. The affine-iota replay always synthesizes the flattened raster index `y * width + x`, so 2D dispatches or workgroups with multiple local invocations write a flat global sequence instead of the component/local index the shader stored.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse ambiguous affine-iota output bindings**

When the store binding is not recovered as a constant, this fallback chooses the first storage-buffer binding without checking that it is the only storage buffer in the set. A valid pipeline layout can contain an unused storage buffer before the actual output binding, so an affine-iota dispatch would write the generated sequence into the wrong VkBuffer instead of the `store_ssbo` destination.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve neighboring data in affine-iota buffers**

For an output SSBO that is a subrange of a larger buffer, mapping that range with `PIPE_MAP_DISCARD_WHOLE_RESOURCE` allows the driver to throw away the entire pipe resource even though this replay only rewrites `total * 4` bytes. That can corrupt unrelated data in the same VkBuffer outside the descriptor range; use a range discard/update here like the const-fill path does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When the other addend is any tracked affine def, this now folds the coefficients without checking that both operands denote the same scalar index. The walk records every component derived from an index intrinsic as `1 * gid + 0` (for example `gl_GlobalInvocationID.y` after a channel/mov, or `gl_WorkGroupID.x` after the new system-value lowering), so kernels such as `out[gid] = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x + gl_GlobalInvocationID.y` in a 1-D dispatch get classified as stride 2 even though `.y` is zero, and `gl_WorkGroupID.x` can be replayed as the per-invocation gid when `local_size_x > 1`. Since `r300vk_affine_iota_dispatch_replay` materializes only the linear invocation index, please only combine the known zero-base intrinsic (or otherwise carry component/system-value identity) instead of treating arbitrary tracked affine operands as the same gid.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep steinmarder bundle names out of Mesa metadata**

AGENTS.md says “MUST keep Mesa normal flows independent of `steinmarder`” and that “steinmarder bundles and findings stay out of Mesa.” These new catalog entries check a steinmarder retained-bundle name into compiled Mesa source, so normal Mesa metadata now carries an external evidence-bundle namespace. Please keep these new `.retained_bundle` fields NULL and record the bundle in commit or review text instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound the stencil version advance before 255**

When the current stencil version is 255, `INCR` is the saturating increment operation (for example, `PIPE_STENCIL_OP_INCR` only updates values `< STENCIL_MAX` in `src/gallium/drivers/softpipe/sp_quad_depth_test.c`), so a successful `EQUAL 255 + INCR` draw reports success but leaves the cell at 255 rather than advancing to `v + 1`. As written, the theorem advertises the primitive for all versions; please either constrain it to `v < 255` or document/use wrap semantics explicitly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a domain whose exact bound covers five-limb columns**

`R300_NUM_DOMAIN_U7_DOT` is defined for the four-term DP4 case with `exact_int_bound = 64516`, but this new op's own theorem relies on five-term convolution columns up to `5 * 127^2 = 80645`. Any admission or audit code that follows the catalog's `op.domain` to the domain descriptor will get an exactness contract that is smaller and different from the operation being cataloged, so this should either get its own five-limb domain/policy or use a domain whose bound matches the stated mechanism.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject swizzled vector affine sums**

When both operands are vector seeds, this combines only `s`/`b` and never checks the ALU source swizzles, so a vector add such as `tmp = id + id.yxz; store tmp.x` is recorded as if each lane were still `2 * unit(lane)`. After a later channel extraction, the classifier can report `2 * id.x` even though the stored value is `id.x + id.y`, letting the affine-iota replay synthesize different buffer contents instead of rejecting the non-canonical vector expression.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the selected vec lane's affine state**

For any `vecN` constructor with a tracked first operand, this records the whole vector using `sc[0]`, so later extracting lane 1 or 2 inherits lane 0's coefficients. For example, a 1D dispatch that stores `vec2(id.x, id.y).y` should write zero for every invocation, but the classifier records the value as `id.x`, causing the affine-iota replay to write a linear ramp instead of rejecting or tracking the second lane.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not coerce zero 3D x stride to one**

For 3D affine-iota kernels whose stored value intentionally has no `id.x` term, this fallback turns `ax == 0` into `stride == 1` before the canonical-flatten check and the fragment constant upload. A shader storing `id.y * tx + id.z * tx * ty` with matching dispatch dimensions then passes validation as if it were the full flattened index, and replay writes values that vary by `x` even though the kernel's value is constant across each x row.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require all log4 loads to use the same SSBO**

For a log4 candidate whose four `load_ssbo` instructions use different bindings but the same 2x2 offset pattern, the detector still admits the kernel and records only `load[0]` as the input binding; dispatch replay then samples that one buffer for all four taps. That changes kernels such as averaging four tiled/source buffers into averaging four texels from the first buffer, while the original shader would have read each binding separately, so this detector should either verify every load binding/base matches `load[0]` or reject the shape.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve constant SSBO offset bases**

When the four loads have the expected 2x2 deltas but start at a nonzero constant byte offset, subtracting the minimum base admits the shader without carrying that base into replay. The runtime path later scans and wraps the input from `desc[0]->buf.offset` and writes the output at `desc[1]->buf.offset`, so a kernel averaging a subregion such as `in[base + ...]` or storing to `out[base + ...]` reads/writes the beginning of the descriptor instead of the shader's addressed range; require zero bases or store and apply them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject swizzled vector SSBO loads**

This match treats any ALU source whose `ssa` is one of the four `load_ssbo` defs as the scalar payload, but NIR sources can select a component of a vector load via the source swizzle while keeping the same `ssa` def. For a shader averaging `.y`/`.z`/`.w` lanes from vector SSBO loads, the detector still admits it, while replay always wraps the bytes as RGBA8 and uses only the R channel, so it averages the wrong component; require scalar 32-bit loads or verify the selected component is the byte lane replay samples.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve bytes outside the log4 output range**

For log4 dispatches that write into a subrange of a larger VkBuffer, mapping the destination with `PIPE_MAP_DISCARD_WHOLE_RESOURCE` can discard bytes outside `desc[1]->buf.offset .. offset + out_total*4`, even though the original `store_ssbo` only updates the addressed output elements. This can corrupt adjacent data or other descriptors sharing the same buffer; use a non-whole-resource write/discard mode unless the entire pipe_resource is being overwritten.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep recovered log4 bindings independent**

If only one of the input/output bindings was captured from NIR and the other was not, this fallback replaces both entries with the first two storage-buffer bindings from the layout. In mixed cases such as a constant input binding plus a descriptor-derived output binding, replay ignores the valid captured binding and can sample the wrong buffer; recover only the missing side, or require both bindings to be captured before using the recorded values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope the PVS failure claim to measured RS482**

AGENTS.md requires known, hypothesized, and speculative claims to be marked distinctly, but this new wording turns one RS482 draw-correlation result into a blanket statement about every RS48x HB_TCL target; `r300_hb_tcl_is_hb_family()` still enables the route for both `CHIP_RC410` and `CHIP_RS480`, so on RC410 (or other unmeasured RS48x variants) the comment now records an unsupported silicon conclusion rather than the measured RS482 fact. Please keep the known RS482 hang separate from any hypothesis about the rest of the gated family.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the RS482 root cause as a hypothesis**

The new comment says the RS482 oracle “falsified” PVS execution, but the observation recorded here is that the PVS upload and draw path is reached and then the first draw hangs before a framebuffer write or fence signal. That does not distinguish “PVS never executes” from a PVS-side hang, bad VAP resource setup, or another hardware-TCL command-stream fault; AGENTS.md requires source comments to keep known observations and implementation hypotheses separate. Please state the measured hang as known and keep “does not execute PVS” as a hypothesis unless there is a decisive execution probe.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope kernel recovery and reboot claims**

This adds an unconditional source comment that `radeon` performs no recovery and that each draw costs a physical reboot, but AGENTS.md requires kernel-facing claims to identify the exact kernel mechanism and keep evidence classes separate. As written, a single observed RS482 run is recorded as a driver-wide recovery property; please scope this to the observed kernel/manual-reset path (or cite the specific `radeon` recovery mechanism that makes it invariant), so future readers do not treat kernel-version-dependent behavior as a silicon fact.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore unused later-subpass input slots**

This rejects any later subpass with `inputAttachmentCount > 0`, but Vulkan allows individual entries in `pInputAttachments` to be `VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED`. A render pass that keeps a fixed input-attachment array shape for compatibility but marks every later-subpass entry unused does not actually read an input attachment, yet this path now fails creation with `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN` in both the 1.0 and 2.0 entry points. Please scan the attachment references and reject only when a non-`VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED` input is present.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use American English in new prose**

`AGENTS.md` requires American English spelling in new or modified source comments. This new comment uses British spelling (`colour`), and there are multiple newly-added occurrences of the same pattern in this diff, so the patch violates the repository's documented review rules; please change these to American English before landing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include depth/stencil in self-dependency rejection**

This helper only checks input attachments against color attachments, but the same unsupported feedback loop exists when subpass 0 uses the same attachment as an input and as `pDepthStencilAttachment`: `r300vk_record_begin_render_pass` binds that attachment as the zsbuf while the lowered `subpassLoad` binds it as a fragment texture. Such a pass now slips past the new correctness-or-reject validation and can still sample stale or incoherent depth/stencil data, so the overlap check should also compare each input ref with `depth_stencil_attachment_ref`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat descriptor set as part of input identity**

This new distinct-input check only compares `data.binding`, so two `subpassInput` variables at `(set=0,binding=0)` and `(set=1,binding=0)` are treated as one input even though they are different descriptors. The replay path also selects input attachments by binding number alone, so in that valid shader shape the pipeline is accepted and both loads read whichever matching binding the replay finds first instead of getting a clean reject.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
